rows.conclusion: Independent 2026-08-10 official-law re-audit retains proposal-only YELLOW. Current Article 499, traceable to Law 13/2020, criminalises personal cannabis consumption, cultivation, introduction and possession. The Government currently publishes a genuinely operational but narrow Sativex/cannabinoid product protocol for qualifying MS-spasticity patients: specialist and commission approval, patient-specific Ministry import, special narcotics prescription and HNSM outpatient dispensing. rows.independent_truth_reason: The Cyprus Ministry of Health Pharmaceutical Services currently publishes a dedicated Pharmaceutical Cannabis Legislation hub and its official-gazette K.D.P. 73/2019 regulations. The official materials prove a pharmaceutical-cannabis regulatory framework but no reviewed source proves a presently operating patient route with an eligible patient, prescriber and actual lawful pharmacy supply. The general enacted/framework-without-operational-patient-access rule gives YELLOW, not GREEN; recreational prohibition does not create a false RED because the medical framework is positively established.

Article 10 prohibits drug-related cultivation, keeping, supply and use in Cambodia unless licensed; Article 11 limits licenses to research, clinical, scientific or industrial purposes, while Article 12 confines Table-I research authorisation to individuals of a state organisation. zero_grey_completion.conclusion_ru: Свежая визуальная перепроверка закрывает объединённый GEO SJ красным без переноса более благоприятного режима только одной физической части. Lov om Jan Mayen §§1–2 визуально подтверждает, что Jan Mayen является частью Kingdom of Norway и что норвежское уголовное право действует там прямо. Правительственный разбор Svalbardloven отдельно визуально подтверждает действие норвежского уголовного права на Svalbard. Действующий правительственный cannabis-раздел прямо объясняет, что оборот наркотиков допускается только для медицинских и научных целей, лечение cannabis регулируется отдельно, а иные dealing, use и possession уголовно наказуемы. Norwegian Medical Products Agency визуально подтверждает ограниченный пациентский путь через Sativex, Epidyolex и named-patient permits. Однако Forskrift 747 §11 прямо распространяет legemiddelloven и apotekloven на Svalbard, тогда как визуально проверенный исчерпывающий §18 для Jan Mayen их не перечисляет. Поэтому recreational prohibition и criminal enforcement доказаны для обеих частей, а ограниченный cannabis-patient pathway — только для Svalbard. По явно обозначенному консервативному общему знаменателю composite GEO получает красный: единого подтверждённого medical-cannabis access, общего для обеих частей, нет. Это не утверждение, что на Jan Mayen отсутствует любая медицинская помощь; это минимальный доказанный общий цвет объединённой ISO-строки.

independent_review.legal_interpretation: SJ is a composite GEO. Norwegian criminal law applies to both Svalbard and Jan Mayen, so the current national prohibition context reaches recreational axes in both components. The current health-law regulation expressly applies the Medicines Act and Pharmacy Act to Svalbard, while its exhaustive Jan Mayen section omits both. The current DMP cannabis protocol proves an operational named-patient, prescriber, pharmacy-delivery, and import route only where the medicines framework applies, therefore on Svalbard. It cannot be presumed to apply to Jan Mayen. The old conservative-intersection Red discarded this proven component divergence, which is forbidden by the general composite resolver. The only honest color for a combined GEO without a single unitary regime is unpainted UNKNOWN.

verified_sources.exact_fragment: Article 2a prohibits cultivation of Cannabis-genus plants. Article 3a prohibits import/export, preparation, sale, delivery, transport, possession, presence and use of hemp extract and tincture. Article 4 prohibits import/export and possession/presence/use of hemp, hemp resin and usual resin preparations including hasjiesj. Article 5 permits prescription only under ministerial requirements for Article 3 and 3a means. Article 7 preserves limited medical professional handling and lawful own medical use exceptions for specified means, not an operational patient programme.

project_comparison.reason: The current official Opiumwet 1960 BES page visibly defines hennep as flowering or fruiting tops of plants of the Cannabis genus, prohibits cultivation of plants of the Cannabis genus, prohibits hemp extract and tincture import/export, preparation, sale, delivery, transport, possession, presence and use, and prohibits hemp, hemp resin and usual resin preparations such as hasjiesj for import/export and possession/presence/use. project_comparison.reason: Independent recheck: Chad Law No. 024/PR/2000 Article 36 adopts ratified international narcotic/psychotropic schedules but delegates possession, prescription and dispensing rules to decrees. The visually reviewed Article 34/36 crop is generic and has no cannabis-specific patient, product, supply or current implementing-decree proof. Article 134 penalizes contravention of regulatory provisions, not cannabis conduct by itself. The INCB Yellow List visibly names cannabis in the international Schedule I, but is international context, not evidence of a current Chadian cannabis regime. Fresh searches of the Chad Official Gazette, Presidency, Health Ministry and decree/order terms found no applicable current cannabis-specific implementing instrument. Therefore the prior limited-lawful Yellow inference mixed schedule adoption, generic prescription delegation and treaty context; neither a lawful route nor full negative proof is established. TD remains proposal-only UNKNOWN; current map RED and SSOT remain untouched.

rows.conclusion: Официальная копия Chad Loi 024/PR/2000 визуально показывает в Article 36, что Республика Чад принимает списки narcotics ратифицированных международных конвенций и регулирует их prescription/dispensing; актуальный официальный INCB Yellow List 64th edition (July 2025), страница 3, визуально включает CANNABIS и CANNABIS RESIN, EXTRACTS and TINCTURES в Schedule I. Journal officiel n° 39-2025: Loi n° 30-2025 du 22 août 2025 relative à la lutte contre la production, la détention, la fabrication, le transport, le trafic et l’usage illicites des stupéfiants, des substances psychotropes et des précurseurs en République du Congo
verified_sources.legal_basis_for_extension: National law of the Republic of the Congo published in the Journal officiel; no Democratic Republic of the Congo, regional or treaty-only substitution.
verified_sources.source_authority: Secrétariat général du Gouvernement / Journal officiel de la République du Congo
verified_sources.exact_fragment: Article 3 defines Table I as high-risk plants/substances without medical interest and Tables II-III as having medical interest. Article 6 prohibits Table I conduct except express authorisation; Article 8 confines the Article 13 ministerial authorisation to medical purposes. Articles 28-31 restrict professional purchase, prescription and retail dispensing to Tables II-III. Article 52 prohibits use outside medical prescriptions. Article 53 penalises illicit personal acquisition, possession or cultivation and expressly lists cannabis oil and other cannabis-plant derivatives as high-risk-drug cases.
verified_sources.annotation: CG is Republic of Congo (Congo-Brazzaville) only. This source must never be associated with CD / Democratic Republic of the Congo.

project_comparison.reason: The official Republic of the Congo government PDF hosted on sgg.cg was opened, rendered and visually reviewed. Page 1 visibly identifies Loi n° 30-2025 du 22 août 2025 in the Journal officiel de la République du Congo and states that the law regulates illicit production, possession, manufacture, transport, trafficking and use of narcotics, psychotropic substances and precursors. Page 2 visibly classifies narcotic/psychotropic plants and substances, states that cultivation of plants classified as narcotics by international conventions is prohibited on national territory, and permits authorization only where substance use is limited to medical purposes. Page 6 visibly states that use outside medical prescriptions of controlled drugs is prohibited and Article 53 gives cannabis-specific personal-use penalty bands for cannabis oil and other derivatives of the cannabis plant. Project recreational=ILLEGAL and enforcement=STRICT are supported, with a personal-use penalty scope note. Project medical=NONE is not changed because the reviewed official source shows only a general prescription/authorization framework for controlled substances and no visible cannabis-specific medical access programme.

rows.conclusion: Independent 2026-08-10 official-law re-audit records current direct cannabis evidence under Republic of the Congo Law 30-2025. It proves illicit recreational use/possession/cultivation restrictions and names cannabis oil/derivatives, but it does not establish cannabis placement in Table I versus Tables II/III or an operational cannabis patient route. Generic medical authorisation and generic Table II/III dispensing cannot bridge that gap. CG is proposal-only UNKNOWN/unpainted, not a legacy RED/YELLOW inference. No SSOT, map, runtime, production or deployment state changed.

independent_truth.legal_reason: Loi 30-2025 is a current, applicable national primary law. It positively proves a prohibition and penalties for illicit cannabis-related possession/cultivation/use. Its prescription, pharmacy and dispensing route is expressly confined to Tables II and III, but the official text reviewed does not identify cannabis or a cannabis medicine in either table and does not establish a patient, prescriber, supply or operational cannabis programme. General controlled-drug prescription wording neither proves patient access nor completes the negative medical axis required for RED. The fail-closed proposal is therefore unpainted UNKNOWN, not RED or YELLOW.

project_comparison.reason: The official local-regulation page for Curaçao's Opiumlandsverordening was opened and visually reviewed. The page visibly states that cultivation of plants of the Cannabis genus is prohibited, prohibits hemp extract and tincture handling, and prohibits hemp, hemp resin and usual hemp-resin preparations such as hashish, esrar, chiras and djamba for import/export and possession/presence/use. Article 7 visibly contains licensed and professional medical-purpose exceptions. The official Ministry of Health, Environment and Nature application form under the Opium Ordinance was also rendered and visually reviewed; it expressly applies to licences to cultivate, produce and/or manufacture cannabis or cannabis material, including cannabis/cannabis resin/cannabis oil for supply to patients or research, and lists licence categories for import, export, transit, cultivation, processing/manufacturing, selling, delivery, transport and possession of cannabis/cannabis oil/resin. Project recreational=ILLEGAL and enforcement=STRICT are supported, but project medical=NONE is contradicted by the official medicinal cannabis/research licensing pathway. The reviewed material supports at least LIMITED medical/research licensing scope, not a broad recreational allowance.

rows.conclusion: Curaçao is visually verified from the official Opiumlandsverordening and official Ministry licence-application material: cannabis cultivation and hemp/hashish possession/import/export/use are prohibited unless licensed or within narrow medical/professional exceptions, while the Ministry form confirms a medicinal cannabis/research licensing path; project medical=NONE is a mismatch.
rows.independent_truth_reason: The current official Curaçao Opium Ordinance defines hemp as Cannabis, keeps Articles 3a and 4 prohibitions current, and permits pharmacists/authorised medicine dispensers to handle the listed substances only for medical purpose and within medicines-law and Ministerial requirements. The official Ministry of Health licence form is cannabis-specific: companies apply to cultivate, produce or manufacture cannabis for supply to patients or research. It is a licensing application and does not prove a licence holder, patient eligibility/registration, or actual dispensing to a patient. The general limited-lawful/special-permit rule therefore produces YELLOW, not GREEN; adult use remains prohibited.

project_comparison.reason: Свежая визуальная перепроверка закрывает BV красным без автоматического переноса всего материкового медицинского режима Norway. Bilandsloven визуально подтверждает норвежский суверенитет над Bouvetøya и прямо распространяет на biland норвежское уголовное право. Официальный government analysis Prop. 69 L подтверждает ту же норму: private law, criminal law и law of procedure действуют на bilandene, а специальное законодательство и подзаконные акты требуют отдельного основания. Действующий правительственный cannabis-раздел визуально связывает cannabis с уголовными §§231 и 162: оборот, передача, пересылка, use и possession вне медицинских/научных целей незаконны. Narkotikaforskriften визуально называет Cannabis и Cannabisharpiks и показывает запрет §5, а Penal Code устанавливает строгие сроки за narcotics offences. Но отдельного акта, распространяющего на Bouvetøya материковый patient-access режим legemiddelloven/DMP, не найдено, и национальная medical-cannabis страница не выдаётся за BV-specific право. Поэтому минимально доказанный территориальный режим: recreational запрещён, criminal enforcement строгий, подтверждённого BV medical-cannabis patient pathway нет. В трёхцветной модели это красный; вывод не утверждает, что на необитаемом острове существует абсолютный запрет любой медицинской помощи.

rows.conclusion: Proposal-only BV=UNKNOWN/unpainted. Current Bilandsloven §2 directly applies Norwegian criminal law to Bouvet Island but requires a King decision for other laws. Current Narkotikaforskriften visibly applies to Norway and lists cannabis as prohibited, while the Norwegian named-patient cannabis route is national context. No current extension order for either special regime to BV is proved. The existing historical RED closure is superseded, not deleted; SSOT, map, runtime, production and deployment remain unchanged; APPLY_ALLOWED=false.

fresh_grey_39_reaudit.visible_conclusion_ru: Второй поиск по Lovdata и regjeringen.no закрыт без недосмотренных кандидатов. Bilandsloven §2 и действующий straffeloven визуально подтверждают применение норвежского уголовного права к Bouvetøya; narkotikaforskriften визуально называет Cannabis и Cannabisharpiks и запрещает их по §5. Но сама narkotikaforskriften и медицинское регулирование помечены как действующие для «Norge», тогда как Bouvetøya — норвежское biland вне Kongeriket Norge, и отдельного акта о распространении legemiddelloven/narkotikaforskriften на Bouvetøya не найдено. Поэтому recreational/enforcement chain сильная, но полный medical-компонент для цветовой модели не доказан: BV остаётся честно серым, а норвежский medical-cannabis режим не переносится автоматически.

verified_sources.legal_basis_for_extension: National Fiji statute.
verified_sources.source_authority: Fiji Ministry of Health and Medical Services
verified_sources.exact_fragment: Section 11(1)(c): "any person may possess such quantities of an illicit drug that have been lawfully prescribed or provided for the purpose of treating a medical condition". Section 11(1)(b) exempts a lawful occupation/profession involving possession, supply or administration for that lawful purpose. Section 11(2) permits the Minister for Health, consulting the Pharmacy and Poisons Board, to license lawful import, export or manufacture of an illicit drug. Cannabis is an illicit drug under Schedule 1; unauthorised conduct remains an offence under sections 4-5.
verified_sources.visual_summary: Rendered official Health Ministry-hosted Act pages visibly show medical prescription/provision exemption and Ministerial licence. PDF capture lacks address-bar chrome; cannabis linkage and currentness are chained through separately recorded official sources.

project_comparison.reason: The official Laws of Fiji / Office of the Attorney-General consolidated Illicit Drugs Control Act 2004 page was opened, the site disclaimer was accepted, and the relevant dynamic sections were visually captured. The act header screenshot visibly identifies the Illicit Drugs Control Act 2004 and the official Laws of Fiji site. Section 4 visibly criminalizes importation or exportation of an illicit drug without lawful authority, with fine up to $1 million or life imprisonment or both. Section 5 visibly criminalizes unauthorized acquisition, supply, possession, production, manufacture, cultivation, use or administration of an illicit drug, and dealings for transfer, transport, supply, use, manufacture, offer, sale, import or export, with fine up to $1 million or life imprisonment or both. Schedule 1 visibly includes Cannabis and cannabis resin, states that Cannabis plant references do not include hemp or hemp-derived plant parts with THC concentration not exceeding 1%, and the captured lower Schedule 1 elements show Cannabis plant, Cannabis seed and Cannabis oil. Section 32A visibly creates a factual presumption that claimed hemp is Cannabis and exceeds 1% THC until the contrary is proved. Project recreational=ILLEGAL, medical=NONE and enforcement=STRICT are supported by the reviewed official evidence; no project status SSOT was changed.

rows.conclusion: Fiji is visually verified from the official Laws of Fiji Illicit Drugs Control Act 2004. Cannabis, cannabis resin, Cannabis plant, Cannabis seed and Cannabis oil are directly covered by Schedule 1, with a low-THC hemp exception and a THC/hemp factual presumption. Unauthorized possession, cultivation, use, supply, manufacture, import/export and related dealings are punishable by up to $1 million fine or life imprisonment or both. Project ILLEGAL/NONE/STRICT matches the reviewed official evidence.

visual_review.visual_summary: All three preserved MSPAS treaty pages were visually read. They name cannabis and treaty duties but remain international context rather than direct domestic cannabis proof.

project_comparison.reason: Independent recheck: Guatemala Decreto 48-92 Article 2 defines drugs generally, including plants or plant parts from which drugs can be extracted and substances under treaties mandatory in Guatemala. Article 3 permits strictly necessary drug activities by legally empowered persons for medical treatment, analyses, research and medicine manufacture, with prescription required for retail sale. Articles 36-39 criminalise unauthorised activity for the same general drug category. The MSPAS-published treaty pages name cannabis but state that each Party must criminalise conduct in its domestic law; they are international context, not a domestic cannabis product, patient or conduct rule. Fresh current MSPAS pages prove an operating generic controlled-substance administration system (company registration, authorised narcotic prescriptions, quotas and import forms), but no cannabis-specific product registration, patient eligibility, dispensing route or cannabis-specific permit was located. The 2026 MSPAS alert title naming illegal cannabis product manufacture/commercialisation was identified, but its scanned text was not readable in this audit environment and is not used as a legal conclusion. Thus the former Yellow/strict-negative inference mixed generic domestic terms, generic operational procedures and treaty text. GT remains proposal-only UNKNOWN; current map RED and SSOT remain unchanged.

rows.conclusion: Guatemala is visually verified through the official SECCATID/OJ Decreto 48-92 anti-narcotics law plus MSPAS-published convention text that explicitly defines cannabis plant and cannabis cultivation control scope. The evidence supports project ILLEGAL/NONE/STRICT, with a caveat that Article 3 contains a narrow general controlled-drug legal-use exception for authorized medical/scientific/medicine-manufacture purposes but does not prove a separate medical cannabis programme.

findings: Current MSPAS pages operate generic controlled-substance recipe authorisation, company registration, quota and import workflows.
Congress record 5224 remains an initiative, not an enacted cannabis law.
No current cannabis-specific product registration, patient route, pharmacy dispensing route, special permit or domestic statute naming cannabis was located.
The MSPAS 2026 alert title is cannabis-specific but its scanned PDF text was not readable; it is retained as unrelied current context only.

verified_sources.title: States of Guernsey - FAQ about cannabis based products medicinal import licences
verified_sources.legal_basis_for_extension: DIRECT_STATES_OF_GUERNSEY_PATIENT_IMPORT_PROCESS_PAGE
verified_sources.source_authority: STATES_OF_GUERNSEY_HEALTH_SOCIAL_CARE
verified_sources.direct_fragment: The official CBPM FAQ says a Bailiwick resident may import prescribed controlled drugs; it links the official import-licence form, describes payment/application and email receipt, states an import licence is normally received in approximately 5-10 working days, requires the clinic/pharmacy to send the prescription to the licensing team, and says the issued licence enables the UK pharmacy to send the shipment to Guernsey.
verified_sources.visual_summary: Live GOV.GG CBPM FAQ visually reviewed with official owner banner, individual import eligibility, official online form, application process and issued-licence supply instructions visible.

project_comparison.reason: The official States of Guernsey pages were fetched successfully as GOV.GG HTML and rendered locally for screenshot review because the live headless browser request was blocked by GOV.GG WAF while curl returned the official page content. The rendered GOV.GG cannabis licensing screenshot visibly states that businesses can apply to cultivate cannabis for cannabis-based products medicinal (CBPM), that successful applicants can cultivate high-THC cannabis plants, that cannabis remains a controlled drug within the Bailiwick, that cultivation is strictly prohibited unless licensed, and that prospective licensees and the public should be aware it is an offence to cultivate any plant of the genus Cannabis except under a relevant local licence. The same visible crop states it is unlawful to possess, supply, produce, import or export cannabis except under relevant local licences. The rendered GOV.GG prescribed medicinal cannabis products page visibly states these are controlled substances obtained by private prescription, that the government complies with the legal process for issuing import licences, that the law in Guernsey allows local doctors to prescribe pharmaceutical-standard products privately, and that islanders may obtain prescriptions from the UK or Jersey and arrange importation into the Bailiwick. It also visibly lists local availability/funding routes for Epidyolex, Sativex applications and Nabilone, and says Bailiwick residents can privately access prescribed cannabis-based products medicinal via an on-island clinic and local pharmacy or through UK/Jersey prescriptions with lawful importation. The GOV.GG FAQ visibly states a personal import licence allows import of prescribed controlled drugs and that only Schedule 2, 3 or 4 controlled drugs under the Misuse of Drugs (Bailiwick of Guernsey) Ordinance 1997 may be imported under this licence. Project recreational=ILLEGAL and enforcement=STRICT are supported, but project medical=NONE is too coarse/outdated because the reviewed official pages show a regulated/private-prescription and import-licence route for prescribed medicinal cannabis products. No project status SSOT was changed.

rows.conclusion: Guernsey is visually verified from official States of Guernsey cannabis licensing and prescribed medicinal cannabis pages. Recreational/general cannabis remains illegal and strict outside licences, but medical=NONE is a project mismatch: official GOV.GG material shows prescribed medicinal cannabis products are controlled substances available through private prescription/local doctor routes and import licences, with limited local availability/funding routes for specified CBPMs. Screenshots were rendered from fetched official GOV.GG HTML because live headless browser access was WAF-blocked.

truth_first_independent_review.legal_interpretation: The patient path is proven cumulatively by current official States of Guernsey pages: prescribed CBPM, a private clinician prescription, a usable official online individual import-licence route, licensing-team processing, and pharmacy dispatch; the same official source documents local clinic/pharmacy access. The separate industry licence route is not relied on for Green. Recreational possession/supply remains prohibited outside licence.

prescriber_route.exact_fragment: Pasal 8(1): Group I narcotics are prohibited for health services; Pasal 8(2) permits only limited scientific/diagnostic/laboratory-reagent use with Minister approval.
prescriber_route.note: Research/reagent approval is not a prescription route.

lawful_supply.exact_fragment: Law 35/2009 Pasal 111, 113 and 114 criminalise unauthorised Group I plant possession/cultivation, production/import/export/distribution and sale/transfer.
lawful_supply.note: No lawful patient supply follows from the direct Group I health-service prohibition; offence provisions separately prohibit unauthorised supply.

pharmacy_or_dispensary.exact_fragment: Pasal 8(1): Group I narcotics are prohibited for health services; Pasal 8(2) permits only limited scientific/diagnostic/laboratory-reagent use with Minister approval.
pharmacy_or_dispensary.note: Permitted scientific/reagent route is not dispensing.

Law 35/2009 Pasal 111, 113 and 114 criminalise unauthorised Group I plant possession/cultivation, production/import/export/distribution and sale/transfer.
import_route.note: The only stated Group I approval pathway is scientific/reagent use, while unauthorised import is criminal; no patient import exception proved.

programme_operational.exact_fragment: Regulation 15/2025 Pasal 1(2): Group I only for scientific development and not used in therapy; Annex Group I item 8 names all Cannabis plants/products including resin and hashish; items 9-10 name THC.
programme_operational.note: A current no-therapy classification cannot constitute an operational patient programme.

programme_commenced.exact_fragment: Pasal 4 brings the classification regulation into force; it establishes no medical cannabis programme and classifies cannabis as Group I not used in therapy.
programme_commenced.note: This axis is about a patient programme, not commencement of the prohibition/classification regulation.

recreational_possession.exact_fragment: Law 35/2009 Pasal 111, 113 and 114 criminalise unauthorised Group I plant possession/cultivation, production/import/export/distribution and sale/transfer. Cannabis is explicitly Group I under current Regulation 15/2025.
recreational_possession.direct_locator: Pasal 111; Regulation 15/2025 Annex Group I item 8
recreational_possession.note: Positive current prohibition evidence, not inference from absence.

recreational_supply.exact_fragment: Law 35/2009 Pasal 111, 113 and 114 criminalise unauthorised Group I plant possession/cultivation, production/import/export/distribution and sale/transfer.
recreational_supply.note: Positive current prohibition evidence for production, import/export, distribution, sale and transfer.

recreational_cultivation.exact_fragment: Pasal 111 criminalises without-authority planting and cultivating Group I narcotics in plant form; Regulation 15/2025 Annex Group I item 8 names Cannabis plants.
recreational_cultivation.direct_locator: Pasal 111; Regulation 15/2025 Annex Group I item 8

penalty_regime.exact_fragment: Pasal 111 sets 4-12 years and fines for unauthorised Group I plant conduct; Pasal 113-114 set higher penalties for unauthorised supply; Pasal 127(1)(a) sets up to four years for Group I self-use.
penalty_regime.note: Rehabilitation in Pasal 127(2)-(3) is a judicial/health consequence for a misuse victim and does not legalise cannabis possession or create patient access.

research_only.exact_fragment: Pasal 8(2) permits Group I only in limited quantities for science/technology and diagnostic/laboratory reagents with Minister approval on BPOM recommendation.
research_only.note: Recorded as a non-patient exception only; it cannot create Yellow or Green.

independent_review.legal_interpretation: Law 35/2009 and Regulation 15/2025 must be read together: the current regulation classifies cannabis, resin/hashish and THC as Group I and says Group I is not therapy; the statute prohibits Group I for health services, reserves a narrowly approved science/reagent exception, and criminalises unauthorised Group I possession/cultivation/import/export/distribution/sale/self-use. Rehabilitation clauses do not repeal the self-use offence and do not create a legal cannabis-medicine route.

legal_conclusion.why_not_green: No operational adult-use or patient-access path; therapy and health-service use of cannabis Group I are expressly excluded.
legal_conclusion.why_not_yellow: Science/reagent approval and rehabilitation are not patient access, decriminalisation, production, cultivation, pharmacy dispensing or a lawful limited cannabis programme.
legal_conclusion.why_red: Positive current applicable evidence proves recreational possession/cultivation/supply prohibitions and cannabis-specific medical/therapy exclusion.

non_inferences: Rehabilitation is not decriminalisation.
Article 8(2) science/diagnostic/laboratory-reagent permission is not patient access.
A 2026 criminal-code transition circular is current enforcement context, not a substitute for the statute or a color rule.

project_comparison.reason: Iraq is visually verified from the Iraqi Ministry of Justice-hosted Official Gazette PDF for issue 4446 containing Law No. 50 of 2017 on Narcotic Drugs and Psychotropic Substances. The PDF was downloaded from moj.gov.iq, rendered and visually inspected. Page 1 visibly identifies the Iraqi Official Gazette issue and Law No. 50 of 2017. Page 4 visibly defines illicit traffic to include cultivation and trade of narcotics and defines possession/acquisition. Page 17 visibly states that cultivation, import, export, possession, acquisition, sale, transport, transfer, exchange, receipt, delivery or mediation of listed plants and seeds is prohibited except for medical or scientific purposes under statutory conditions, and the listed plants visibly include cannabis plant. Page 19 visibly punishes cultivating, trafficking or trading narcotic-producing plants or seeds outside permitted cases and Article 28 visibly sets life or temporary imprisonment and a large fine for relevant narcotics/plants acts. Page 16 visibly allows possession of personal medical treatment containing narcotic or psychotropic substances for health reasons within doctor-prescribed quantities. Page 26 visibly provides a treatment-diversion caveat: no criminal case for people who voluntarily seek treatment, with observation/treatment periods. Project recreational=ILLEGAL, medical=NONE as a cannabis patient-program status, and enforcement=STRICT are supported, with caveats for medical/scientific authorization, doctor-prescribed medicine possession, and voluntary treatment diversion. No project status SSOT was changed. Independent 2026-08-10 review adds proposal-only YELLOW based on Article 23’s cannabis-specific medical/scientific exception; no live layer was captured, so no map/SSOT mismatch is asserted.

rows.conclusion: Iraq is visually verified from the Iraqi Ministry of Justice Official Gazette PDF for Law No. 50 of 2017. The reviewed screenshots directly show cannabis plant in the prohibited-plant provision, strict penalties for narcotic-producing plants and relevant narcotics/plants acts, and caveats for medical/scientific authorization, personal prescribed medicine, and voluntary treatment. Project ILLEGAL/NONE/STRICT is supported with those caveats. Independent 2026-08-10: YELLOW proposal only. Article 23 is cannabis-specific limited lawful authority, while Arts. 18-20 cannot be inflated from generic controlled-medicine prescription/pharmacy rules into operational cannabis patient access. Art. 40 is not decriminalisation. No map, SSOT, runtime, production or deployment state changed.

verified_sources.exact_fragment: Latest official Criminal Code edition 56638 dated 24 July 2026: Article 282 punishes illegal manufacture, acquisition, storage, transport, sending for sale, production or sale of narcotic drugs; Article 283 punishes illegal non-sale conduct at large or especially large quantities. project_comparison.reason: Kyrgyzstan is visually verified from the Kyrgyz Ministry of Justice centralized legal information bank (CBD) official API/rendered law content. The official frontend was WAF-protected during capture, so the accepted screenshots are local renders of official CBD API content with the frontend and API URLs shown in the header, analogous to rendering an official downloaded law document for visual inspection. The controlled-list screenshot visibly lists cannabis oil, cannabis resin/hashish, cannabis straw, cannabis straw concentrate/marihuana, extracts and tinctures. The size-criteria screenshots visibly list cannabis oil, cannabis resin/hashish, cannabis straw, cannabis straw concentrate/marihuana, extracts/tinctures and Cannabis (hemp), including thresholds such as Cannabis (hemp) 80 / 80-2400 / 2400. The Criminal Code current edition screenshot visibly shows Chapter 36 and Articles 282 and 283 punishing illegal narcotic-drug/psychotropic-substance/analogue sale scope and large non-sale scope with imprisonment/fine bands. Law No. 69 of 2024 screenshots visibly show the narcotic-drugs law title, prescription acquisition of medicines containing narcotic drugs/psychotropic substances in pharmacies, enforcement bodies, destruction of wild living organisms containing narcotic drugs/psychotropic substances, and confiscation. Project recreational=ILLEGAL and enforcement=STRICT are supported. Project medical=NONE is retained as a cannabis patient-program status because reviewed sources show general narcotic-medicine prescription/dispensing caveats, not a regulated cannabis patient-access programme. No project status SSOT was changed.

rows.conclusion: Kyrgyzstan is visually verified from official Kyrgyz Ministry of Justice CBD API-rendered law content. Screenshots show cannabis/hashish/marihuana/cannabis plant in the controlled list and size thresholds, Criminal Code Articles 282/283 penalties for narcotic-drug sale and large non-sale scope, and Law No. 69 prescription/enforcement/destruction caveats. Project ILLEGAL/NONE/STRICT is supported with general narcotic-prescription and threshold caveats.

recreational_possession.exact_fragment: Article 283 punishes illegal acquisition, storage, transport or sending of narcotic drugs at large and especially large quantities; active Resolution 152 provides cannabis thresholds.

recreational_supply.exact_fragment: Article 282 punishes illegal acquisition, storage, transport, production and sale of narcotic drugs; active List I supplies cannabis-family coverage.

penalty_regime.exact_fragment: Article 282 provides five-to-eight, eight-to-twelve and twelve-to-fifteen year sanction bands; Article 283 provides a fine or up to five years, then five-to-ten years at especially large quantities.

patient_eligible.exact_fragment: Article 24 applies to medicines containing narcotics but does not identify a cannabis medicine, patient condition or cannabis registry.

prescriber_route.exact_fragment: The current prescription rule is generic to medicines containing narcotics; it does not establish that a cannabis-family substance is an authorised medicinal product.

lawful_supply.exact_fragment: Article 24 describes pharmacy dispensing of eligible narcotic-containing medicines, but no active cannabis product registration, lawful cannabis supply or import route was found in fresh official search.

pharmacy_or_dispensary.exact_fragment: The law names pharmacies generally but neither a cannabis product nor an operating cannabis dispensing route.

programme_operational.exact_fragment: The active List I controls cannabis-family substances but provides no patient registry, application route, clinic or dispensing programme.

evidence_notes: The active 2025 cannabis list is List I (limited circulation/special control), not a List IV prohibition for human use.

A generic controlled-narcotic prescription rule cannot itself establish cannabis medicine availability. Fresh official health/medicine-register searches located registration systems but no cannabis product or patient route; absence of a search result was not treated as a prohibition.

final_visual_acceptance.reason: Fresh official API metadata establishes active document status and latest edition IDs. Exact law fragments were rendered from the official API response with the endpoint visible in the capture header and visually reviewed.

project_comparison.reason: Lebanon is visually verified from official Ministry of Public Health law/schedule PDFs and official Presidency of the Council of Ministers context. The MOPH Narcotics page screenshot visibly lists Law No. 673 issued on 16 March 1998 related to narcotic drugs, psychotropic substances and precursors and an updated version of attached tables related to Narcotics Law No. 673/98. rows.conclusion: Lebanon is visually verified from official MOPH Law 673 and updated schedule PDFs plus official PCM Law 178 context. project_comparison.reason: Liberia is visually reviewed from official Executive Mansion and Ministry of Justice sources, but no live official direct cannabis-specific statutory text was confirmed in this pass. The Executive Mansion screenshot visibly states President Weah signed the Control Drug and Substance Act of 2023 into law, describes the Act as regulating/restricting/controlling/eradicating illegal narcotic substances, and visibly describes penalties for unlicensed import and manufacture of controlled drugs or substances, including non-bailable drug offenses and 10-to-20-year penalty bands. The Ministry of Justice 2015 Annual Report PDF was downloaded from moj.gov.lr and rendered locally; screenshots visibly state that passage of the Drug/Controlled Substance Act in 2014 created the legal framework for investigation/apprehension/prosecution/sentencing, that LDEA arrested 115 persons in violation of the Controlled Drugs and Substance Law and seized 5,112.7 kg of marijuana, and that specific marijuana trafficking/possession cases were charged and processed to court. Additional screenshots visibly show marijuana as the leading seized drug, major marijuana farming/cultivation activities, marijuana farms burned and plants seized, and implementation challenges around the Controlled Drugs and Substance Act of 2014. This supports project recreational=ILLEGAL and enforcement=STRICT as official context. The reviewed official material does not show a medical cannabis patient-access program, so project medical=NONE is not contradicted. Because the direct cannabis-specific statutory schedule/text was not live-confirmed from an official host, the row is kept context-only rather than treated as a direct law page. No project status SSOT was changed.

rows.conclusion: Liberia is closed as visually reviewed official context-only evidence. Executive Mansion screenshots confirm the 2023 Control Drug and Substance Act and strict controlled-drug penalties, while Ministry of Justice report screenshots show the 2014 Controlled Drugs/Substance Act framework, marijuana seizures, marijuana trafficking/possession prosecutions, and marijuana farming/cultivation enforcement. This supports project ILLEGAL/NONE/STRICT as official context, but direct cannabis-specific statute text was not live-confirmed from an official host. No project status SSOT was changed.

independent_review.legal_conclusion: The official evidence proves historical marijuana enforcement and 2023 enactment of a general controlled-drug law, but no current cannabis-specific schedule/operative clause or current medical-patient exception was located. A full negative conclusion would be an absence-of-evidence inference.

verified_sources.currentness: Official Ministry page retrieved HTTP 200 on 2026-08-10; a later official Law No. 19/1425 amendment was separately reviewed for penalties. No repeal or separate operational patient programme was asserted from this source.

rows.conclusion: LI independent legal truth is GREEN. Current official BMG/BMV pages establish cannabis Schedule d, a restricted medical exception, patient-specific permission, prescriber route and pharmacy dispensing; the official 2025 Government report records 20 Dronabinol/Cannabis medical-use permits. Direct visual access to that report remains Cloudflare-blocked and is honestly marked as strict visual-acceptance pending. No SSOT, map, runtime, production or deployment value was changed.

independent_review.legal_interpretation: Current BMG forbids cannabis at or above 1 percent THC but authorises a restricted medical exception. Current BMV makes that exception patient-specific, authorises a doctor prescription for Schedule d, and authorises pharmacy dispensing. The Government 2025 report states that the Office of Public Health authorises such prescriptions and issued 20 Dronabinol/Cannabis medical-use exceptions in the reporting year. These independent official sources aggregate to a proven operational patient route. This is GREEN under the project policy despite recreational prohibition; it is not adult-use.

rows.conclusion: MG independent legal truth is UNKNOWN and unpainted. Current official Law 97-039 directly proves national cannabis-plant cultivation prohibition and cannabis-specific illicit personal-consumption penalties. The separately found Health Code only supplies generic controlled-substance special-authorisation/prescription wording; it neither proves a cannabis patient route nor a cannabis-specific medical prohibition. Under the general no-generic-minister-permission and no-false-RED rules, RED and YELLOW are both unproven. No SSOT, map, runtime, production or deployment value was changed.

independent_review.legal_interpretation: Law 97-039 proves national adult cultivation prohibition and illicit cannabis-derivative personal-consumption penalties. The Code de la Santé’s generic medical/scientific authorisation text cannot be silently applied to cannabis, and no cannabis-specific special-authorisation implementation or express medical exclusion was proved. The resulting uncertainty blocks both a limited-lawful color and a full negative color.

verified_sources.title: Malaysia Attorney General's Chambers - Dangerous Drugs Act 1952, Act 234, updated text as at 4 July 2023

project_comparison.reason: Malaysia is visually verified from the official Attorney General's Chambers Laws of Malaysia PDF for Dangerous Drugs Act 1952, Act 234, updated as at 4 July 2023. The screenshot/readable extract visibly defines cannabis and cannabis resin, identifies dangerous drug as a substance in the First Schedule, restricts possession of cannabis, applies the Act's prepared-opium control provisions to cannabis and cannabis resin, lists cannabis/cannabis resin in the First Schedule, creates a trafficking presumption for 200 grammes or more of cannabis, cannabis resin, or their combined weight, and shows Section 39B trafficking in dangerous drugs punishable with death or imprisonment for life and whipping if not sentenced to death. This supports project recreational=ILLEGAL and enforcement=STRICT. Project medical=NONE is not contradicted: the reviewed Act contains general registered-medical-practitioner and traveller medicinal-preparation contexts for dangerous drugs, but no regulated cannabis patient-access program was visually confirmed. No project status SSOT was changed.

rows.conclusion: Malaysia is closed as visually verified official cannabis-law evidence. The official AGC Dangerous Drugs Act 1952 PDF visibly defines cannabis/cannabis resin, restricts possession, applies cannabis/resin controls, lists cannabis in the First Schedule, sets a 200g trafficking presumption and Section 39B death/life/whipping trafficking penalties. This matches project ILLEGAL/NONE/STRICT with registered-medical-practitioner and traveller-preparation caveats. No project status SSOT was changed.

independent_review.conclusion: Historical official primary-law captures and the currently hosted MOH cannabis FAQ prove cannabis-specific recreational possession/cultivation restrictions and show that the cited cultivation exception is limited to a Minister-authorised public officer. The FAQ also states that cannabis medical products require registration, but its no-registered-product statement is dated 2020. No current 2026 official patient, prescriber, dispensing, import or registered-product route was positively proved; neither does the record affirmatively prove that every medical route is absent. The independent proposal therefore remains UNKNOWN/unpainted, not RED or YELLOW.

project_comparison.reason: Mauritius is visually verified from the official Laws of Mauritius current Dangerous Drugs Act PDF and the official National Assembly Dangerous Drugs (Amendment) Act 2022. The current Act screenshots visibly define gandia as Cannabis Sativa L or Cannabis Indica plant parts, hashish/charras/chiras as resin obtained from the cannabis plant, Indian hemp as dried flowering or fruiting tops of the cannabis plant, and medicinal cannabis as a cannabis-plant product. Section 5 visibly prohibits cultivation of the cannabis plant. Section 6 visibly prohibits producing, manufacturing, distributing, transporting, possessing, supplying, transferring, purchasing, using, importing, exporting or transiting First Schedule plants/substances/preparations; the First Schedule visibly lists Cannabis/Gandia/Indian Hemp excluding medicinal cannabis and Cannabis Resin excluding medicinal cannabis. The current Act also visibly contains Part IIA - Medicinal Cannabis: authorised patient, authorised specialist/pharmacist, specific therapeutic conditions, lawful use/importation only under Part IIA, regional-hospital Medicinal Cannabis Therapeutic Committee, request/approval/prescription/dispensing/register/importation rules, Ministry/police supervision, and a foreign-patient possession exception; the Second Schedule visibly lists Medicinal cannabis. Therefore project recreational=ILLEGAL is supported, but project medical=NONE is contradicted and should be reviewed as LIMITED/REGULATED. Project enforcement=SOFT is partially supported only for personal-consumption drug users because Part IIIA and section 59B visibly allow rehabilitation in lieu of prosecution where there are no aggravating circumstances and the user is not a trafficker; cultivation, unauthorised possession/use/import/export and Part II/IIA contraventions remain offences. No project status SSOT was changed.

rows.conclusion: Mauritius is closed as visually verified official cannabis-law evidence. The official current Dangerous Drugs Act directly defines cannabis/gandia/Indian hemp/hashish, prohibits recreational/general cannabis cultivation and First Schedule cannabis conduct, and also creates a regulated medicinal cannabis framework through Part IIA and Second Schedule medicinal cannabis. Project recreational=ILLEGAL is supported, project medical=NONE is a mismatch, and project enforcement=SOFT is only partly supported for personal-use rehabilitation/non-prosecution while unauthorised cannabis conduct remains offence-based. No project status SSOT was changed.

project_comparison.reason: Mexico is visually verified from official Orden Jurídico Nacional current consolidated Ley General de Salud and Código Penal Federal PDFs plus the official Diario Oficial medical-cannabis regulation PDF. The Ley General de Salud screenshots visibly show Article 235 subjecting seeding, cultivation, harvesting, preparation, acquisition, possession, commerce, transport, prescription, supply, use and consumption of narcotics to the health-law framework and Secretaría de Salud authorization; Article 235 Bis requiring public policies to regulate medicinal use of pharmacological derivatives of cannabis sativa, indica and americana or marihuana, including THC, and national research/production; Article 245's industrial exception for cannabis derivatives with 1 percent or less THC and broad industrial uses; Articles 477-479 creating penalties for unauthorized non-commercial possession above the table context but no criminal action for a consumer or dependent person who possesses table amounts for strict personal consumption outside specified places, with Cannabis Sativa, Indica or Mariguana listed at 5 grams; and the SCJN Declaratoria General de Inconstitucionalidad 1/2018 invalidating the absolute administrative prohibition on Health Secretariat authorizations for cannabis and THC self-consumption with recreational purposes. The DOF regulation screenshots visibly establish the health-control regulation for production, research and medicinal use of cannabis and pharmacological derivatives, define cannabis and cannabis medicines, require permits for sowing/production for research/fabrication, and create special prescription, pharmacy/botica, patient registry, possession and international-travel rules for cannabis medicines. The Código Penal Federal screenshots visibly retain prison penalties for narcotics production/transport/traffic/supply/possession and marihuana cultivation, while stating marihuana sowing/cultivation/harvesting is not punishable when carried out for medical and scientific purposes under federal authorization. This supports project recreational=ILLEGAL only with explicit self-consumption authorization and 5g no-prosecution caveats, supports medical=REGULATED, and supports enforcement=SOFT for strict personal-use threshold while retaining strict penalties for trafficking, supply, unauthorized cultivation and possession outside those caveats. No project status SSOT was changed.

rows.conclusion: Mexico is closed as visually verified official cannabis-law evidence. Official OJN Ley General de Salud, DOF medical-cannabis regulation, and OJN Código Penal Federal screenshots show a regulated medical cannabis framework, a 5g strict-personal-consumption non-prosecution threshold, SCJN recreational self-consumption authorization caveat, and continuing offence/penalty provisions for unauthorized trafficking, supply, cultivation and possession outside the narrow personal-use/medical-scientific authorization contexts. Project ILLEGAL/REGULATED/SOFT is supported with these caveats; no project status SSOT was changed.

project_comparison.reason: Morocco is visually verified from official ANRAC-hosted Bulletin Officiel PDFs. Loi n° 13-21 page 1 visibly promulgates the law relative aux usages licites du cannabis, defines cannabis, cannabis plant, cannabis flowering/fruiting tops, cannabis resin, narcotic and industrial purpose, and Article 3 requires ANRAC authorization for cannabis cultivation, production, nurseries, seed/plant import/export, transformation, fabrication, transport, commercialization, product export and product import. Article 5 visibly limits cultivation/production authorization to quantities needed for medical, pharmaceutical and industrial products. Page 2 Article 6 visibly states that cultivation/production authorization for cannabis varieties whose THC content exceeds the regulatory threshold can be granted only for medical and pharmaceutical industries. Page 3 Article 17 visibly prohibits manufacturing products exceeding the THC threshold except medicinal and pharmaceutical products. Page 6 visibly gives ANRAC control/reporting functions and includes measures aimed at ending illicit cannabis uses. Page 9 Article 50 visibly applies Dahir n° 1-73-282 sanctions/security measures to unauthorized cannabis culture, production, transformation, fabrication, transport, commercialization, export/import and seeds/plants import, while Articles 51-55 add prison/fine/confiscation and doubled recidivism penalties for violations of the licensed framework. Décret n° 2-22-159 visibly implements Loi 13-21, limits cultivation/production authorization to Al Hoceima, Chefchaouen and Taounate, creates application/committee/ANRAC procedures, and sets stock/THC/traceability-related implementation rules. This supports project recreational=ILLEGAL, medical=REGULATED and enforcement=STRICT with the caveat that the law creates licensed medical/pharmaceutical/industrial cannabis channels rather than general recreational legalization. No project status SSOT was changed.

independent_review.legal_interpretation: Independent official-law conclusion: Morocco has a current, applicable licensed cannabis regime. Law No. 13-21 and Decree No. 2-22-159 establish ANRAC authorization, cultivation/production/processing/commercialisation and a restricted medical, pharmaceutical, and industrial purpose. Current ANRAC operational material also regulates pharmacies, parapharmacies, and dedicated stores for direct consumer sale of lawful cannabis products. This proves a limited lawful cannabis regime and therefore YELLOW. It does not prove GREEN: no reviewed official source establishes a named cannabis medicine plus patient eligibility, an individually lawful clinical prescription route, and medicine-specific dispensing/import as one current operational patient-access chain. The 2026 ANRAC CBD/registration/recommendation pages are retained as context and are not promoted to a patient programme.

project_comparison.reason: Mozambique is visually verified from an official Supreme Court of Mozambique PDF, Acórdão Proc. nº 31/2022-P. Page 1 visibly shows República de Moçambique / Tribunal Supremo and a criminal appeal summary for tráfico e consumo de estupefacientes, stating that possession of 232 bolinhas of cannabis sativa commits the small-quantity trafficking offence under Article 36 of Lei nº 3/97 of 13 March, and that Article 55 possession/consumption requires proof that the drug was sufficient for three days of personal consumption. Page 6 visibly states that laboratory testing was positive for cannabis sativa, that the 590g substance falls within Table I-C annexed to Lei nº 3/97, and that commercialization of cannabis sativa was prohibited and criminally punishable. Page 7 visibly quotes Article 33 of Lei nº 3/97, punishing unauthorized cultivation, production, fabrication, extraction, preparation, sale, distribution, purchase, transfer, transport, import, export or illicit possession outside Article 55 of listed plants/substances with 16 to 20 years major imprisonment; the same page quotes Article 55, punishing consumption or own-use acquisition/possession of listed plants/substances with up to two years imprisonment and a corresponding fine. Page 10 visibly applies Article 36 small-quantity trafficking to 590g cannabis sativa with an abstract penalty range of 2 to 8 years major imprisonment and fine. Page 11 visibly states that although cannabis sativa is a so-called soft drug, in Mozambique its consumption continues to be absolutely prohibited and trafficking is more gravely censured. This supports project recreational=ILLEGAL and enforcement=STRICT with a small-quantity-trafficking classification caveat. Reviewed official sources did not visually confirm any cannabis medical patient program, so project medical=NONE is not contradicted. No project status SSOT was changed.

rows.conclusion: Mozambique is closed as visually verified official cannabis-law evidence from the official Supreme Court PDF applying and quoting Lei nº 3/97 to cannabis sativa. The reviewed screenshots visibly show cannabis sativa classified in Table I-C, consumption absolutely prohibited, Article 33 trafficking/unauthorized cannabis conduct with 16-20 years major imprisonment, Article 55 own-use consumption/possession up to two years plus fine, and Article 36 small-quantity trafficking applied to 590g cannabis sativa with 2-8 years imprisonment plus fine. Project ILLEGAL/NONE/STRICT is supported, with a caveat that the strongest official source is a Supreme Court statutory-application PDF rather than a consolidated legislative portal page; no project status SSOT was changed.

independent_review.status_reason: Current official Supreme Court text directly identifies cannabis sativa as Table I-C under Lei nº 3/97, quotes Article 55 criminalising consumption and own-use acquisition/possession of Tables I-IV substances, and states cannabis consumption remains absolutely prohibited in Mozambique. Article 33 authorisation language controls supply-side conduct and supplies no patient entitlement. Fresh official-domain checks found no later cannabis-specific medical exception, patient programme, registry, medicinal product, dispensing route or amendment replacing this rule.

project_comparison.reason: Nauru is visually verified from the Republic of Nauru / Department of Justice and Border Control Illicit Drugs Control Act 2004 consolidation and the official RONLAW Illicit Drugs Control (Amendment) Act 2024. The consolidation title page visibly states Republic of Nauru and that the consolidation is prepared and published in a legislation database by the Department of Justice and Border Control under the Legislation Publication Act 2011. Page 7 visibly criminalizes unlawful possession, manufacture, cultivation, use, administration, supply and dealing in any illicit drug. Page 28 visibly lists Cannabis and cannabis resin in Schedule 1 - Illicit Drugs. Page 31 visibly lists Cannabis fruit, Cannabis plant, Cannabis seed and Cannabis oil as other illicit drugs. The official RONLAW 2024 amendment title page visibly states No. 24 of 2024, certified 23 December 2024, and amends the Illicit Drugs Control Act 2004; page 5 visibly inserts Section 6A for unlawful manufacture, cultivation and supply/dealing with life imprisonment and at least 10 years without parole/probation, and amends Section 7 to the same life-imprisonment standard. This supports project recreational=ILLEGAL and enforcement=STRICT, with a stricter-2024-penalty caveat. Page 8 of the consolidation visibly includes international traveller prescribed-drug and general lawful occupation/minister-license exemptions for illicit drugs, but no cannabis-specific patient access programme was visually confirmed, so project medical=NONE is not contradicted but needs a general medical/licensing exemption caveat. No project status SSOT was changed.

rows.conclusion: Nauru is closed as visually verified official cannabis-law evidence. Official/DJBC Act 2004 screenshots visibly list cannabis and cannabis resin, cannabis plant, seed, fruit and oil in the illicit-drugs schedules and criminalize unlawful cannabis-related possession/manufacture/cultivation/use/supply/dealing because those are illicit drugs. The official RONLAW 2024 amendment visibly updates the current penalties, including life imprisonment with at least 10 years without parole/probation for manufacture/cultivation/supply/dealing conduct. Project ILLEGAL/NONE/STRICT is supported, with caveats for the 2024 strict penalty update and general prescribed-drug/licensing exemptions that do not prove a cannabis patient programme. No project status SSOT was changed.
rows.independent_conclusion: Independent proposal-only YELLOW. Cannabis/resin is expressly an illicit drug, while the same preserved current Act permits any person to possess an illicit drug lawfully prescribed or provided for treating a medical condition and exempts lawful professional possession/supply/administration; it also retains medicinal import licensing. The certified 2024 amendment strengthens prohibition penalties but does not amend Sections 14 or 48. No current official product, register, named licence, pharmacy stock, dispensing or operational programme is proven, so Green is not derived. The old medical=NONE conclusion is not independently provable as a complete medical-negative axis.

project_comparison.reason: Nepal is visually verified from the official Nepal Law Commission Act and its embedded Government of Nepal PDF. The preserved primary pages visibly define cannabis and medicinal cannabis as narcotic drugs, prohibit non-exempt cannabis cultivation, production, purchase, sale, import, storage and use, and impose cannabis-specific penalties. Fresh current Nepal Law Commission publication of the prevailing Act confirms Section 5: treatment use is not prohibited where an approved physician recommends a narcotic drug and the person buys the recommended quantity from a licensed shop. Because Section 3 expressly defines medicinal cannabis as cannabis extract or essence, this prescription exception applies to scheduled cannabis; it is not a treaty-only or generic controlled-drug inference. No current official source independently proves a registered cannabis product, active patient registry, dispensing outlet, import route or operational patient programme. Project medical=NONE therefore omits a proven limited lawful cannabis prescription exception, while project recreational=ILLEGAL and enforcement=STRICT remain supported. No project status SSOT was changed.

rows.conclusion: Independent current official-law re-audit: Nepal has a direct cannabis prohibition with cannabis-specific penalties, but the same current Act creates a limited cannabis-applicable prescription exception. Section 3 defines medicinal cannabis as cannabis extract or essence, and Section 5 permits treatment use where an approved physician recommends the narcotic drug and the person purchases the recommended quantity from a licensed shop. That satisfies the project YELLOW prescription/special-permit semantics but does not prove an operational cannabis patient programme or adult-use. The retained primary visual evidence confirms the cannabis definition and prohibition; the current Section 5 text was reopened semantically and direct visual crop remains pending. Proposal-only `NP=YELLOW`; SSOT, map, runtime, production and deployment remain unchanged.
rows.independent_conclusion: The current official Act proves a limited cannabis-applicable prescription exception, not an operational patient programme. Section 3 defines medicinal cannabis as cannabis extract or essence; Section 5 permits treatment use where an approved physician recommends a narcotic drug and the person buys the recommended quantity from a licensed shop. The patient and prescriber legal axes are proven, but current official evidence does not independently identify a registered cannabis product, operating licensed shop, active dispensing or programme. The general rule therefore derives YELLOW, not GREEN or RED.

verified_sources.title: Puerto Rico OGP Biblioteca Virtual - Ley 42-2017 Ley MEDICINAL cannabis medicinal
verified_sources.note: Official Puerto Rico Office of Management and Budget / Biblioteca Virtual PDF. Visual review confirms Ley Num. 42 de 9 de julio de 2017, Ley MEDICINAL, revised 15 April 2024. Visual review confirms the Act amends Title 19 of the Virgin Islands Code to expand legalization of cannabis from medicinal use to include Adult Use Cannabis; chapter 34 is the Virgin Islands Cannabis Use Act; section 775 establishes a regulated system for cultivation, manufacture and sale of cannabis for adult, medicinal and sacramental use; section 779 protects Qualified Patients and sets medical possession/cultivation limits; section 785 permits adults over 21 to possess up to two ounces of cannabis, fourteen grams of cannabis concentrate and one ounce of cannabis products; section 806/807 style penalty pages retain penalties for conduct outside the chapter; and section 6 states compliant chapter 34 cannabis possession/commercial cannabis activity is not a violation of Title 19 chapter 29 section 607a.

verified_context_sources.title: Office of Cannabis Regulation, U.S. Virgin Islands - 2024 VICUA Rules and Regulations public PDF
verified_context_sources.note: Official OCR PDF labelled Proposed Rules and Regulations for the VI Cannabis Use Act. Visual review confirms the rules cite statutory authority under 19 V.I.C. section 777, define Act as V.I. Act 8680 / Virgin Islands Cannabis Use Act codified in Title 19 chapter 34, define Adult-Use/Adult User as use of cannabis by persons over 21 pursuant to the Act, restate adult-user possession limits, set rules for adult-use lounge/cannabis-use permits and unlawful actions/penalties, and include Lieutenant Governor certification that the regulations were duly published and comply with formatting requirements. This is retained as regulatory context; Act 8680 remains the direct law source.

project_comparison.reason: U.S. Virgin Islands is visually verified from official OCR Act 8680 / Virgin Islands Cannabis Use Act. Project recreational=ILLEGAL is contradicted because the Act visibly expands legalization from medicinal use to include Adult Use Cannabis and section 785 permits adults over 21 to possess limited amounts of cannabis, cannabis concentrate and cannabis products. Project medical=NONE is contradicted because the Act visibly preserves and regulates qualified medical cannabis patients, medical cannabis patient cards, medical possession limits and personal medicinal cultivation. Project enforcement=STRICT is too broad as a blanket status: the official law creates a regulated legal adult/medical/sacramental framework and retains penalties only for unlicensed, false, unauthorized or otherwise unprotected conduct. This is recorded as a status mismatch finding and does not mutate project status SSOT.

rows.conclusion: U.S. Virgin Islands is closed as visually verified direct official cannabis-law evidence. Official Act 8680 creates the Virgin Islands Cannabis Use Act, expands legalization from medicinal to adult-use cannabis, establishes regulated adult/medicinal/sacramental cannabis systems, permits adult 21+ possession limits and regulated qualified patient medical possession/cultivation, while preserving penalties for conduct outside the Act. Project ILLEGAL/NONE/STRICT is a direct mismatch against the official law. No project status SSOT was changed.

verified_sources.title: Vatican City State - Legge N. VIII: Norme complementari in materia penale
verified_sources.note: Official Vatican City State PDF, Legge N. VIII: Norme complementari in materia penale, 11 July 2013. Visual review confirms Title IX on offences involving narcotic or psychotropic substances; Article 41 defines narcotic and psychotropic substances by reference to UN convention tables and lists; Article 42 punishes unauthorized cultivation, production, manufacture, extraction, refining, sale, offer, transfer, distribution, commerce, transport, procurement, transit and delivery of narcotic or psychotropic substances and specifically includes cultivation of the Indian hemp plant (pianta di canapa indiana) for narcotic production, with imprisonment and fines; Article 44 provides aggravating factors plus confiscation and destruction of narcotic or psychotropic substances; Article 45 applies penalties to abusive non-therapeutic medical prescriptions and excludes pharmacy acquisition/sale/transfer in medicinal dose and form on the basis of medical prescriptions.
verified_sources.legal_basis_for_extension: DIRECT_VATICAN_CITY_STATE_PRIMARY_PENAL_LAW
verified_sources.direct_fragment: Article 42 criminalises unauthorised narcotic/psychotropic conduct and expressly includes Indian-hemp cultivation for narcotic production; personal-use quantities remain punishable. Article 45(2) excludes only pharmacy acquisition and medicinal-dose/form transactions on medical prescriptions. The exception is generic to narcotic/psychotropic medicines and contains no cannabis product, patient eligibility, cannabis prescriber or cannabis supply evidence.

current_reopen_2026_08_08.legal_effect: Does not alter the previously visually read Article 42/45 text. It cannot upgrade a generic prescription exception to cannabis access or prove the absence of a cannabis-specific exception.
